articles.title: Simulations reveal how a solar vortex and reconnecting magnetic fields can launch a rotating jet
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Solar spicules are slender jets commonly found in the chromosphere. They lift relatively cool plasma from the lower solar atmosphere, carry energy upward, and in some cases rotate as they evolve. Small-scale vortices also occur frequently between convection-driven granules in the photosphere. Two questions remain incompletely answered: how these photospheric vortices help form spicules, and how much mass and energy the rising jets carry into the corona.

articles.title: Without marine life, atmospheric CO₂ would shoot up by up to 65% by the end of the century
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Without marine organisms transporting carbon into the deep ocean, the accumulation of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere would be drastically higher in the year 2100, reaching levels between 35% and 65% higher than projected. This is one of the main conclusions of the new policy brief developed within the framework of the European OceanICU project, which was presented at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye.

articles.title: Structural agility of 2D crystals enables digital doping of graphene superlattices
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: A study published in Nature has demonstrated that applying an electric field can switch the atomic arrangement in a stack of two-dimensional (2D) crystals, accompanied by an unusual charge behavior. This provides a new experimental platform for exploring how the structural and electronic properties of atomically thin materials interact.

articles.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
articles.summary: Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron. Physicists trapped a positron and cooled it to temperatures near absolute zero. Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter. Team will conduct most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Any difference between the electron and positron could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics.

articles.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
articles.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.
